title: Validate a finding adversarially without dropping a proven P1
prompt: You are the validator in a findings pipeline, not the author of the claim. Candidate finding: an endpoint concatenates a request parameter into a SQL statement. A reproducer shows that 3 of 20 crafted inputs return rows from another tenant. A reviewer argues that a web application firewall in front of the service probably stops this. Test the claim against its counter-arguments and give your decision, severity and the impact stated as a ratio. Do not claim to have run anything beyond the evidence supplied.
rubric: Tests the claim against its counter-arguments: reach, preconditions, downstream controls, scope and a simpler explanation.
Treats the unverified firewall argument as something that can lower confidence at most, not as grounds to drop a proven P1 finding that has a reproducer.
Keeps the finding and reports it as P1 or High.
States the impact as 3 of 20 inputs and says how that was established.
Does not invent evidence, such as a firewall rule set or extra test runs.
acceptance: Every rubric item must be independently satisfied with evidence.
